name: Wesley Hunt
contest: Texas U.S. Senate — Republican Primary, March 3, 2026
incumbencyStatus: current U.S. House member (TX-38, 2023–present); challenger in Senate race

priorRoles: U.S. Army Captain, Apache helicopter pilot (2004–2012); one deployment to Iraq (55 combat missions), two deployments to Saudi Arabia as diplomatic liaison officer
Candidate for TX-7 (2020 — lost general election to Lizzie Fletcher)
biography.education: B.S. Leadership and Management with Mechanical Engineering, U.S. Military Academy at West Point (2004)
biography.background: Born and raised in Houston, TX. Attended St. John's School (private). Baptist, attends Champion Forest Baptist Church. Commissioned Army 2004. West Point graduate and combat veteran. Self-styled 'Energy Congressman of the World.' Vice Chairman, House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Energy and Mineral Resources (118th Congress). Also served on House Judiciary and Small Business Committees. Announced Senate candidacy October 2025, joining incumbent Cornyn and AG Paxton in primary.
biography.campaignTheme: Frames himself as the most Trump-aligned, next-generation MAGA figure. Core pillars: border security, energy dominance, uncompromising 2A stance, fiscal conservatism via DOGE. Attack vector against Cornyn centers on BSCA gun bill and immigration compromises.
biography.pollStanding: ~26% in latest polling (3rd behind Paxton ~38%, Cornyn ~31% as of Feb 2026); runoff likely if no candidate exceeds 50%
biography.fundraising: $2.0M raised as of February 2026 (vs. Cornyn $11.2M, Paxton $5.9M). Third-highest House recipient of oil and gas money in cycle ($415,445 per E&E News). Allied super PAC 'Standing for Texas' spent ~$4.1M on his behalf.

campaignWebsite.notes: Direct page fetch unavailable; content reconstructed from search result snippets, VoteSmart Political Courage Test responses, and multiple interview quotes referencing the page.

statedPositions.quote: fighting alongside President Trump to deploy our military to the border, label Mexican Drug Cartels as Terrorists, and support Tom Homan in his efforts to deport Biden's illegal immigrants. In favor of construction of a wall and other necessary infrastructure on the border.
statedPositions.notes: Consistent across homepage, issues page, multiple interviews, and introduced legislation (TPS Reform Act, Guaranteeing States Protection Against Invasion Act). Corroborated by Tier 1 vote: YES on HR2 Secure the Border Act 2023.

statedPositions.quote: As the Energy Congressman of the World, I fully understand the importance of Oil and Gas in America's future. Our leaders should be focused on energy addition, not energy transition. The United States produces the cleanest and safest oil and gas found anywhere in the world and we should be drilling more of it, not less.
statedPositions.notes: VoteSmart Political Courage Test response. Repeated verbatim in Hart Energy interview (2022) and campaign stops (2026). Corroborated by LCV 0% lifetime.

statedPositions.quote: No compromise. Absolutely zero compromise. I will not compromise our Second Amendment rights. My first act as senator would be to repeal the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act.
statedPositions.notes: Introduced H.R.6035 Second Amendment Restoration Act (Nov 2025) to repeal red flag incentives and NICS funding from BSCA. Centerpiece attack on Cornyn.

statedPositions.quote: I am Pro Life and believe each life is a precious gift in the image of God. As your Congressman, I will protect the rights of the unborn. Life begins at conception. Fight to protect the sanctity of life. Stop late-term and taxpayer funded abortion, with exceptions when the life of the mother is at risk or in the cases of rape and incest.
statedPositions.notes: VoteSmart Political Courage Test. Consistent with voting record: cosponsor Born-Alive Act, 0% Reproductive Freedom for All, 100% NRLC, SBA Pro-Life endorsement.

statedPositions.quote: Introducing free market reforms into the healthcare system to increase competition to drive the cost of care down, with policy purchase across state lines, increasing transparency in the system and greater flexibility in coverage plans.
statedPositions.notes: Campaign language is softer than OnTheIssues characterization ('taxpayer-funded health care should be abolished in all forms, and Medicaid and Medicare should be de-funded'). Voting record supports harder position: voted to block ACA subsidies, voted to block health care price control measures (DSCC). Scored on voting record over campaign language.

statedPositions.quote: Supported DOGE from day one and voted to codify the wasteful spending that DOGE uncovered. Fighting alongside President Trump to codify DOGE cuts, secure our border, and fight for economic prosperity for all Texans.
statedPositions.notes: Voted AGAINST Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 as insufficiently conservative on spending. Supports Balanced Budget Amendment. Heritage Action 96%. Signals harder-line fiscal conservatism than GOP establishment.

statedPositions.quote: Our men and women in blue risk their lives every day to keep our communities safe. I will stand with them against the radical liberals in the Senate seeking to defund them.
statedPositions.notes: Campaign language only. Separately co-led bipartisan Safer Supervision Act (criminal justice reform bill with rehabilitation focus) — see positionConflicts.
Paraphrase from aggregator site; no specific bill cited. Consistent with CPAC 97% and opposition to CRT in schools.

statedPositions.quote: Opposes COVID-19 vaccine mandates for healthcare workers; opposes mandatory COVID vaccinations generally.
statedPositions.notes: Co-sponsored Freedom for Health Care Workers Act (HR 497) to eliminate HHS vaccine mandate on Medicare/Medicaid facilities. Campaign specifically lists 'mandatory COVID vaccinations' as part of 'Woke Mind Virus' problem.

statedPositions.quote: Weaning the world off of coal and unleashing US LNG will do more to reduce our carbon footprint than any solar or wind project could accomplish.
statedPositions.notes: Consistent framing used through 2026. Introduced Protect LNG Act 2025, pushed FERC on Rio Grande LNG permits.

votingRecord.attendanceRate: 79.2% overall (missed 350 of 1,681 roll call votes, Jan 2023–Feb 2026; GovTrack median for serving members is 98.0%). From Dec 18, 2025–Feb 25, 2026: missed 69 of 89 votes (78%) due to Senate campaign travel. Drew significant scrutiny from Cornyn camp.
votingRecord.ideologicalPosition: Hard-right Republican. CPAC lifetime 97%; Heritage Action 118th Congress 96%; LCV lifetime 0%; AFL-CIO 6-10%.

keyVotes.bill: H.R. 2 — Secure the Border Act of 2023
keyVotes.notes: Requires 900 miles of border wall, mandatory detention for expedited removal subjects, expands ICE capacity, reopens closed ICE detention facilities. Strongly restrictionist enforcement measure.

keyVotes.bill: H.R. 2494 — POLICE Act of 2023 (Protect Our Law Enforcement with Immigration Control and Enforcement)
H.Con.Res. 21 — Direct Biden to remove U.S. troops from Syria
keyVotes.notes: Among 47 Republicans voting for this measure. Non-interventionist lean on this specific vote; consistent with broader America First foreign policy framing.

keyVotes.bill: Fiscal Responsibility Act of 2023 (bipartisan debt ceiling deal)
keyVotes.notes: Among 71 House Republicans opposing — considered deal insufficiently conservative on spending cuts. Signals harder fiscal line than GOP leadership.

keyVotes.bill: H.R. 26 — Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act (118th Congress)
keyVotes.notes: Requires medical care for infants born alive after abortion attempt. Strong pro-life signal beyond standard abortion restrictions.

Absent when House passed 3-year ACA subsidy extension with 17 Republicans joining Democrats. DSCC characterized as 'refusal' to act. Context: Hunt was missing ~78% of votes during this period. Most TX Republicans voted No on the bill itself.

keyVotes.bill: Vote to block bipartisan effort to stop healthcare price spikes (118th Congress)
keyVotes.notes: Voted against price-control related healthcare measure. Source is partisan (DSCC) but documents a specific vote.

keyVotes.bill: H.R. 497 — Freedom for Health Care Workers Act
keyVotes.notes: Would eliminate HHS COVID-19 vaccine mandate on Medicare/Medicaid-certified healthcare facilities.

legislation_introduced.bill: H.R.6035 — Second Amendment Restoration Act (119th Congress, Nov 2025)
legislation_introduced.description: Would repeal firearm-related provisions of the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act: eliminates federal incentives for states to enact red flag laws, cuts NICS background check expansion funding. Introduced as direct campaign contrast with Cornyn.

Reduces legal uncertainty around LNG development by insulating LNG permits from NEPA and Natural Gas Act litigation; establishes 90-day statute of limitations for legal challenges; requires expedited judicial review of LNG-related lawsuits.

legislation_introduced.bill: Guaranteeing the States Protection Against Invasion Act (2026)
legislation_introduced.description: Codifies Trump's border invasion proclamation; authorizes president to declare invasion at southern border; bars immigration relief for those entering during declared invasion.
Eliminates Temporary Protected Status designations for certain countries; tightens statutory limits on TPS program.

legislation_introduced.bill: Safer Supervision Act (co-led with Rep. Jackson Lee and Sen. Coons; bipartisan)
legislation_introduced.description: Reforms federal supervised release: allows courts to grant early termination based on good conduct and restitution payment, reallocates supervision resources to highest-risk individuals, promotes rehabilitation and reintegration. Hunt quote: 'pro-rehabilitation legislation better allocates resources for reintegration into society, it helps to remove the permanent scarlet letter of incarceration, and it creates positive incentives that encourage true rehabilitation.' Backed by conservative (AFP, Club for Growth, CPAC, America First Policy Institute) and progressive (Drug Policy Alliance, Sentencing Project, ACLU) groups simultaneously.
legislation_introduced.notes: IMPORTANT nuance for scoring justice_sentencing_goals axis: this bill is meaningfully toward rehabilitation end of spectrum, atypical for a 97% CPAC-rated member. However, it is sentencing administration reform, not decriminalization or mandatory minimum repeal.

legislation_introduced.bill: CORE Act (Comprehensive Offshore Resource Enhancement) — passed House Natural Resources Committee
legislation_introduced.description: Expands offshore energy resource development. Passed favorably out of committee in 118th Congress.

legislativeSponsorship.notes: GovTrack did not produce a leadership/ideology score for Hunt due to insufficient bill sponsorships for reliable statistical comparison — his record is shorter (one full term) and attendance-reduced.

positionConflicts.topic: criminal justice / sentencing — Safer Supervision Act vs. law enforcement rhetoric
positionConflicts.conflict: Campaign website and public statements exclusively emphasize 'back the blue,' opposing defunding. But Hunt co-led the Safer Supervision Act with Democrat Sen. Coons, which uses rehabilitation-focused language ('remove the permanent scarlet letter of incarceration,' 'true rehabilitation') and creates early-release pathways. This is backed by progressive criminal justice groups alongside conservative ones. Not a direct contradiction — bill targets sentencing administration (supervised release), not decriminalization or abolition — but it meaningfully complicates a pure 'punishment-first' characterization on the justice_sentencing_goals axis.

Hunt calls for 'permanent abolition of DEI' and markets himself as anti-woke. A Dec 2025 opponent ad surfaced records from his time on St. John's School board showing the school implemented DEI curriculum redesigns during his tenure. Hunt's campaign stated he pushed back internally and ultimately resigned rather than 'legitimize woke nonsense.' Controversy used by Cornyn camp in 'Woke Wesley Hunt' ads. For scoring purposes, his stated anti-DEI position and voting record are unambiguous.

positionConflicts.topic: healthcare — campaign softening vs. voting record
positionConflicts.conflict: Campaign website uses moderate 'free market competition' framing for healthcare. OnTheIssues characterizes stated position as 'taxpayer-funded health care should be abolished in all forms, and Medicaid and Medicare should be de-funded.' Voting record (blocking ACA subsidies, blocking healthcare price controls) aligns with harder position. Per scoring methodology, voting record takes precedence over campaign language.

evidenceSummary.overallConfidence: HIGH for climate, firearms, abortion, immigration, and broad fiscal conservatism. HIGH for healthcare model (policy direction is clear even if softened in campaign language). MEDIUM for specific healthcare cost-control. LOW-MEDIUM for justice sentencing (Safer Supervision Act creates genuine nuance). NO EVIDENCE for all three housing axes.
evidenceSummary.notes: Hunt's record is highly consistent across every measured dimension: maximum conservatism on energy/climate (LCV 0%), guns (GOA A, BSCA repeal pledge), immigration (HR2 yes, invasion legislation), fiscal (Heritage 96%, Fiscal Responsibility Act no), and abortion (NRLC 100%, Reproductive Freedom 0%). The AFL-CIO 6-10% and Chamber of Commerce endorsement create the expected economic policy framing. The only substantive complexity is the Safer Supervision Act, which is a genuine bipartisan rehabilitation-leaning criminal justice bill — the scorer should note this rather than placing Hunt at the pure retribution pole of justice_sentencing_goals. The DEI school board controversy does not affect policy axis scoring. High vote-absence rate (78% in 2026) limits the 119th Congress voting record as evidence, but the 118th Congress record is solid and the campaign platform fills the gaps.
